note.title: Predator-prey relationships and adaptations
note.overview: Predator and prey populations cycle with a time lag; structural, behavioural and physiological adaptations affect survival.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 vocabulary for predator-prey relationships and adaptations.
Apply the knowledge rather than relying on recognition alone.
Use the command word and include every required scientific point.
mustMemoriseRules: Prey rise first; predators rise after a time lag; more predators reduce prey; less prey then reduces predators.
Structural is physical, behavioural is an action, physiological is an internal process.
Camouflage, large snow feet, hunting behaviour and venom are different adaptation examples.
